In the bustling halls of a typical high school in modern Earth, Eon was just another ordinary student—average grades, a few close friends, and a passion for video games and light novels about isekai adventures. He often daydreamed about being transported to another world, wielding unimaginable powers, and living a life far removed from exams and part-time jobs. Little did he know, fate—or perhaps some cosmic joke—had plans for him. One rainy afternoon, while crossing the street lost in his thoughts, a truck veered out of control. In a flash of pain and darkness, Eon's life ended... only to begin anew.

He awoke not in a hospital or the afterlife, but in the warm, confining embrace of a womb, birthed into a world of medieval fantasy. The kingdom of Eldoria stretched vast and proud, its borders guarded by rugged villages like Aetherford, a humble settlement nestled between dense forests and the jagged peaks of the Whispering Mountains. It was here, in a modest wooden cottage on the village outskirts, that Eon was reborn as the second child of Lirael and Thorne.

Lirael was a vision of ethereal beauty, with flowing auburn hair that cascaded like autumn leaves and eyes the color of deep emeralds. She had once been a traveling herbalist before settling down, her gentle hands skilled in brewing potions and tending to the sick. Thorne, her husband, was the village's strongest fighter—a broad-shouldered man with a scarred face from years of fending off bandit raids and wild beasts. His black beard was streaked with gray, and his calloused hands wielded a sword with the precision of a master. Their first child, a daughter named Aria, was a lively one-year-old with curly locks inherited from her mother and a spark of curiosity in her wide blue eyes.

From the moment Eon drew his first breath, his mind was crystal clear. Memories of his past life flooded in—school, friends, the accident—intermingled with an instinctive understanding of this new world. Languages, customs, even the faint hum of magic in the air; it all made sense. But he was no fool. Crying like a newborn, he flailed his tiny limbs and cooed innocently, hiding the sharp intellect behind babyish gurgles. His parents beamed with joy at their new son, naming him Eon after an ancient legend of eternal cycles.
